minor.issue: Spec says 'truncates query to 120 chars and source to 40 chars' but Pydantic Field(max_length=120/40) rejects oversized inputs with HTTP 422 instead of truncating. The truncation in route code (q[:120], source[:40]) is dead code — never reached for oversize input. Either remove max_length from Pydantic Field (rely on slicing) or update spec to say 'rejects oversized'.

action_items: Decide truncation contract: either remove Pydantic max_length from SearchLogIn (so q[:120]/source[:40] truncation actually runs) OR update spec/documentation to declare 422 on oversize. Recommend removing max_length since the route code already slices — current behavior contradicts the documented test case.

rca of the issue: Truncation bug RCA — backend/routes/search_analytics.py defines `query: str = Field(..., max_length=120)` and `source: str = Field(default='landing', max_length=40)`. Pydantic v2 enforces max_length at model validation BEFORE the route handler runs. Therefore the slicing on lines 56-58 (`q[:120]`, `(payload.source or 'landing')[:40]`) is unreachable for oversized inputs — they get rejected with 422 first. Reproduction: POST /api/public/search-log with query of 200 chars → 422. Mitigation: remove max_length from Field declarations OR change spec to expect 422. Recommend removing max_length so author's intent (graceful truncation) actually happens.
